I went to Glasgow expecting to deploy the emergency snacks. Glasgow had other plans.

Scotland's biggest city scored 8/10 on my GF safety scale — I tested 10 restaurants and two of them scored a perfect 5/5. The evidence:

→ Glasgow Cathedral — 12th century, free to visit, and best seen from the Necropolis above it. Gothic drama: 10/10. My calves on that hill: less enthusiastic.
→ Red Onion — a full dedicated GF menu, a dedicated fryer, and a chef who comes out to talk allergies with you. There's a GF Sunday roast with GF Yorkshire puddings. I think about those Yorkshire puddings weekly.
→ The Necropolis — a Victorian cemetery on a hill with the best view in the city. Slightly morbid as a highlight? Perhaps. Worth it anyway.
→ Browns — Coeliac UK accredited, the gold standard for celiac safety in the UK. The staff literally ask if you're coeliac. I nearly proposed.
→ Where to stay: The Z Hotel — compact, modern, right by George Square, everything walkable. Which matters, post-Necropolis hill. Booking link is in the guide.
→ The Mural Trail — giant street art all over the city centre. Free, outdoors, and impossible to eat wrong. My favourite kind of attraction.

Also in the full guide: the rest of the 10 restaurants (including proper GF fish & chips), and the UK tip that actually works — say "coeliac," not "gluten-free." Staff take you twice as seriously.

The full Glasgow guide — every restaurant, GF score, and map — is on the site (link in bio). My one Glasgow regret: I ran out of time for the Kelvingrove Museum. Learn from my mistakes.

What's the sight you still regret missing on a trip? Mine still stings a little.
